papers.title_en: Finding Change in Satellite Archives from Text: How to Combine Before-and-After Images Efficiently
papers.authors: Simon Roy, Mark Bong, Giovanni Beltrame
papers.evidence: 面向文本引导变化检索，高效融合前后卫星影像对
papers.tldr: 地球观测应用需要根据自然语言描述检索双时相卫星图像对，融合模块的速度决定了搜索成本。本文使用固定CLIP编码器和统一训练配方，系统比较了注意力、Mamba和Temporal Bottleneck Fusion（TBF）三类融合设计。结果表明，训练免费的两阶段搜索在LEVIR-CC上达到或超过全融合召回，查询成本降低10-15倍，在Dubai-CC上也有相当表现；Mamba在常规patch数下受内存带宽限制，没有线性复杂度优势；TBF压缩参数2.3倍、延迟1.6倍，但过度压缩会悄悄丢失变化相关细节。该研究为卫星变化检索的融合模块提供了基准与高效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Operational Earth observation increasingly calls for answering queries such as ``find the image pairs where a new building appeared.'' This means searching an archive of before-and-after (bi-temporal) satellite image pairs and ranking each pair by how well it matches a natural-language description of the change. The component that performs this match, the fusion module that combines the ``before'' and ``after'' views, must be run at query time across many candidate pairs, so its speed largely sets the cost of every search. We present a controlled comparison of how to build that module. Using one fixed image encoder (a frozen CLIP model) and one training recipe for all variants, we evaluate eight designs drawn from three families: attention, state-space models (Mamba), and learned compression (our Temporal Bottleneck Fusion, TBF). Each design is tested on two benchmarks (LEVIR-CC and Dubai-CC) with ten random seeds, so the reported differences are statistically grounded. We outline three findings: first, a training-free two-stage search (a cheap difference model that shortlists candidates, followed by attention fusion that re-ranks them) matches or exceeds full-fusion recall on LEVIR-CC while cutting query cost $10$-$15\times$, with comparable R@1/R@5 on Dubai-CC; second, the linear-time scan of Mamba, attractive on paper, gives no speed benefit at the patch counts typical of vision transformers ($L{=}196$): the scan is limited by memory bandwidth, whereas attention maps cleanly onto parallel hardware; and third, compressing the fused representation (TBF) reduces parameters by $2.3\times$ and latency by $1.6\times$ for a change-only BLEU-1 cost of $0.007$, although more aggressive compression quietly discards change-relevant detail that aggregate metrics fail to reveal.
